title: Qualify a prepared proposal before it says Ready
baseline_ref: brief/foundations (D-01 and F-01); Q-13 merges after F-01

status.capability_ready: validator and dry runner only; preparedOpportunities stays unsupported until F-09 registers a provider that uses them

ownership.independent_reviewer: pending; Lapo coordinates technical review and shared-file integration

behavior: qualifyPreparedProposal(request, services) returns ready, blocked or review_needed with coded one-line reasons and the exact snapshot judged: proposal revision, flow, version, version digest, bindings and a fingerprint of request plus observed facts.

Source access and required account/target: every connection and machine the graph binds must be available, shown on the proposal and unchanged. Connection lookups are project-scoped and metadata only. Machines are looked up as dispatch looks them up (sidecars only; id, name, unique partial name) and must offer the tool's capability.

Exact version: the live digest(version.trigger), the identity the effect boundary records, must equal the pinned one; versionReadiness must pass; the composition record must be VALIDATED and named by the flow; the goal must be active at the prepared revision.

Deliveries need a real recipient, read per action from the verified manifests: an empty list (which readiness accepts), a missing prop or a whole-value placeholder blocks; a reply, saved draft or edit is addressed by the message it continues, a forward is not.

Authority behavior is predicted with the effect boundary's own fold for the workflow principal, with tool params read as readiness and the engine read them. A refusal blocks; CODE, ungoverned pieces, agents, nested workflows, values computed at run time and time-of-day Authority rules need review.

Typed job constraints: review_before_effects (every opportunity kind) blocks sends, deletions and other external or irreversible effects that would run unasked, and sends shared third-party writes that run unasked to review; forbid checks every category a step reaches; recipients and unverified.

Previews: the basis must be backed by evidence; every effect is described once; 'asks first' must match Authority; 'simulated' needs the dry sample to reach the step; 'completed' needs a succeeded effect record and the step's own SUCCEEDED status from a full run proven to be this version.
recheckQualification returns stale when the fingerprint changes; briefReadiness maps only a current ready qualification to F-01 ready.

PreparedDryRunner runs the exact version once in the real engine on a fixture with every reachable service simulated and no connection resolvable, on a scratch copy deleted afterwards with its run and log file, never through the job queue. Community pieces, CODE and the validate fixture piece are refused. A graph it supports needs a successful sample before Ready.

Both modules are in the #573 workflow data-plane inventory (src/workflows/adapters/untrusted-reach.test.ts): the qualification module reads graph, ids, states, effect digests and step statuses, never payloads; the dry runner returns its own simulated run's bounded step outputs to a person-facing preview, which a model consumer must frame. effect-capabilities.ts exports the tool-to-capability mapping it already used.

migration: None. No schema, data, route or daemon wiring change; nothing calls the validator until F-09.
rollback: Revert the Q-13 commits. No other code references the new modules, the capability export changes no behavior, and there is no schema or data change.
limitations: Only typed constraints are checked; free-text conditions need an unverified constraint.
Placeholder recipients are whole values from a fixed list; recipients computed at run time are checked at dispatch.
A delivery outside the verified adapters, or a tool that sends, has no recipient model and needs review.
A tool step that names no machine is routed at dispatch; that choice is not part of the proposal.
A connection's revision excludes its updated time so token refreshes do not invalidate proposals; re-authorizing a different account under the same row is not detected.
A dry run shows the version executes on its fixture, not that a real model's draft is good; Q-01 and Q-02 measure that.
found: Readiness treats an empty required collection as present, so a Gmail send with receiver [] passes readiness. That is deliberate for collections in general; Q-13 blocks it for deliveries and leaves readiness unchanged.

The engine resolves a {{connections.x}} reference in any step input and interpolates the decrypted credential (checked against the real engine). Readiness blocks this for production, because the connection must belong to the step's piece; the dry runner skips readiness, so it now resolves no connection.
CI's first run on the PR skipped the four real-engine dry-run tests, because they ran before any test had built the engine bundle; they now build it themselves, as evaluation/engine.test.ts does.

review.result: An independent code review found 6 blocking and 10 minor issues. All are fixed in 0dc04964; each code fix has a test that fails when it is reverted.
blocking: S1: the dry runner resolved stored credentials, and the validate fixture piece, treated as pure, returns its connection's token
C1: tool params given as JSON text were judged as {}, so a shell-startup write passed as a plain file write
C2: a LOCKED version overrode effect records naming an older graph; single-step test runs and dispatch authorization counted as verified completion
C3: recipients were read per piece, not per action: a forward with no receiver passed and four verified delivery actions could never be Ready
C4: review_before_effects let third-party writes that reach people, such as calendar invites, run unasked
T1: several safety claims had no test that failed on revert
minor: write_file body computed at run time (C9)
missing tool reported as an Authority refusal (D1)
implementer named by tool instead of by line (D3)
